teaser.en: Convulsions were blamed on a bird called *pungu*, and this aromatic shrub was said to drive it away.

summary.en: *Muurusa pungu* is an aromatic shrub of the coastal bushland. It is used to cure convulsions, which are believed to be caused by a bird called *pungu*.

about.en: *Muurusa pungu* is an aromatic shrub of the mint family, with leaves in opposite pairs that release a scent when crushed.

uses.en: It is used to cure convulsions.

culture.en: The name means 'scare off *pungu*'. *Pungu* is a bird believed to cause convulsions, and this plant is believed to drive it away. Convulsions in Digo belief are often tied to birds: the 'rib' convulsions treated by *mbavubavu* are called *nyuni wa mbavu*, *nyuni* meaning bird.

names.en: The Digo name is *muurusa pungu*, which Duruma shares. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Premna hildebrandtii*.

reason.en: Premna chrysoclada, same genus, also used against convulsions
Aromatic shrub of the same mint family

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
